text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Friday.

LONDON - British stocks recovered some of their poise after sharp falls earlier in the week but still closed lower for a fifth day amid domestic political worries and fears of rising interest rates. The FTSE 100 index ended 3.3 points lower at 4,254.8, falling 169.5 from a week ago.

FRANKFURT - German market trade ended with the DAX index firmly in positive territory, having caught up with its electronic IBIS counterpart. The market had little difficulty shaking off fears of interest rate hikes in the United States and a slide on Wall Street overnight. The DAX-30 index ended at 3,298.24, up 33.57 points and down 61.05 on the week. In after-market trade, the DAX index stood at 3,288.52. PARIS - French stocks cloosed

with a gain of more than 1 percent but off the day's best levels, prices retreated in the late afternoon as the Dow softened and the dollar consolidated some of its gains. The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 33.41 points, or 1.31 percent, at 2,587.13, a fall of 58.49 from last week.

ZURICH - Swiss shares ended 1 percent higher in a recovery from Thursday's marked losses, but dealers said the correction may not yet be over. "The rebound we saw today has not been very convincing," one trader noted, adding that volume remained rather low. But the firming tendency in the U.S. dollar and in bond futures was seen underpinning the market. The Broad Swiss Performance Index advanced 25.98 points, or 0.92 percent, to end at 2,854.64, down 79.22 from last Friday.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended higher as investors, resuming trade after a public holiday, stepped up buying of banking-sector shares that had suffered heavy selling in the past few months. The 225-share Nikkei average added 139.45 points, or 0.75 percent, to finish at 18,633.16. up 709.52 from a week ago.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks shrugged off the day's losses to end up, lifted by bargain hunting in the property sector after selling during most of the week pulled stock prices down to oversold levels. The Hang Seng Index rose 16.97 points, or 0.14 percent, to 12,489.30, falling 247.23 from last week.

SYDNEY - Australian stocks ended weaker after swinging around all day on rumours of bank takeovers, the digestion of the market bellwhether BHP result and in anticipation of a hike in U.S. interest rates. The All Ordinaries index ended 4.90 points lower at 2,386.40, down 36.80 from seven days ago.

JOHANNESBURG - The South African stock market was closed for a National Holiday. On Thursday, gold stocks ended stronger on a recovery in the bullion price, and industrials were soft amid a lack of interest. The All-share index was down 0.9 points at 7,098.6, a fall of 28.5 from last Friday, the Gold index gained 6.6 points to 1,832.2, rising 423.9 from a week ago, and the Industrial index shed 20.0 points to 8,322.6, a drop of 4.6 on the week.
